visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately shows the projectile path, axes, launch angle, and velocity components in the correct relative positions, while Lesson 2’s mid-lesson Desmos view has undefined/erroring equations, no visible trajectory, and a graph scale that would not represent the actual range.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed fill-in gate wired after act_introduction with a real prompt, accepted answer, hint, success message, and remediation path, while Lesson 2 has no gate specs or plan JSON, so it provides no functional interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 is generally clear and naturally paced despite one awkward/misleading range sentence, while Lesson 2 has noticeable narration defects including an unnecessary repeated sentence, calculator-click instructions read as narration, and an abrupt unrelated fragment at the end.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 at least provides timed visual cues that mostly align with the narrated references, despite some missing cues for equations and identities, whereas Lesson 2 has no beat/timing data at all, making its visual-narration synchronization unverifiable and effectively weaker on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly builds the concept through velocity decomposition, vertical time-of-flight, and constant horizontal motion, while Lesson 2 gives the right numerical endpoint but mostly relies on graphing/clicking in Desmos with little explanation and an irrelevant abrupt ending.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has larger, more legible text and a more readable central workspace, while Lesson 1’s mid-lesson diagram and labels are tiny, low-contrast, and pushed into the lower-left with excessive empty space despite its cleaner title screen.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: five of six agents favored it, all with high confidence, across the most substantive dimensions—visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and conceptual accuracy. Lesson 2 only won polish with moderate confidence, mainly for larger, more legible text, but this does not outweigh its major issues: broken or undefined visual graphing, lack of functional interactivity, weaker narration, no timing data, and much thinner conceptual explanation. The weighted consensus strongly favors Lesson 1.
